title: "API Reference"
subtitle: "Python API"

## Public API

These are the names `spice_kernel_db` exports, and the list `spice_kernel_db.__all__` carries. They are the stability promise: within a major version they keep their names and the meaning of their arguments, so a dependent such as planetarypy can pin `spice-kernel-db>=0.23,<1`. Everything else in the package (`spice_kernel_db.db`, `.remote`, `.config`, `.cli`) is internal and may change in any release.

```python
from spice_kernel_db import (
    # the database
    KernelDB, RegistryRow,
    # one call against the configured database
    check, get, metakernels_covering, register_metakernel, resolve_metakernel, scan,
    # configuration
    Config, ConfigError, ensure_config, kernel_roots, add_root, remove_root,
    # metakernel files
    parse_metakernel, parse_metakernel_text,
    # exceptions
    AmbiguousKernelRoot, AmbiguousMetakernel, ConcurrentModificationError,
    LegacyDatabaseFound, MetakernelNotTracked, MetakernelUnreachableError,
)
```

The library is quiet: no function or method prints unless you hand it a `rich.console.Console` (`KernelDB(console=...)`, `get(console=...)`), and warnings go through the `spice_kernel_db` logger, so a script sees them only if it configures logging. The CLI is this API plus a console and one log handler.

### One call against the configured database

```python
resolve_metakernel(ref, mission=None) -> Path
metakernels_covering(body_id, et=None, mission=None) -> list[dict]
check(ref, *, mission=None, hash_=False, remote=False, spice=False) -> dict
get(ref, *, mission=None, yes=False, download_dir=None, force=False, console=None) -> dict
scan(directory=None, *, mission=None) -> int
register_metakernel(path, *, mission=None, official=True) -> dict
```

Each opens the database named in the config, does one thing and closes it; for several operations in a row keep a `KernelDB`. `get` takes a URL or any reference to a tracked metakernel (then it re-fetches from the stored source); without `yes=True` and without a console to ask on it downloads nothing and returns `aborted: True`. `scan` with no directory indexes every configured root and returns the number of files registered. `register_metakernel(official=False)` marks a metakernel assembled locally, such as the output of NAIF's subsetter. The methods behind them are `resolve_metakernel`, `metakernels_covering`, `check_report`, `get_metakernel` / `update_metakernel`, `scan_directory` / `scan_roots` and `import_metakernel` below.

## `KernelDB`

```python
from spice_kernel_db import KernelDB
```

The main class. Wraps a DuckDB database and provides all scanning, lookup, and rewriting operations.

### Constructor

```python
KernelDB(
    db_path: str | Path | None = None,
    read_only: bool = False,
    kernel_roots: list[str | Path] | None = None,
    console: rich.console.Console | None = None,
)
```

`console` is the one place the instance writes to: status tables, notes, progress bars and the download question of `get_metakernel`. Without one (the default) nothing is printed, progress bars are off and every question is answered no, so a script passes `yes=True` where it wants a download. The CLI passes its own console. Warnings go through the `spice_kernel_db` logger either way.

Opens (or creates) the database at the given path. When `db_path` is `None` (the default), the path is loaded from `~/.config/spice-kernel-db/config.toml`; without a config file it is `~/.local/share/spice-kernel-db/kernels.duckdb`. The schema is initialized automatically (unless `read_only=True`).

Before 0.21.0, a database found only at the pre-0.19 default `~/.spice_kernels.duckdb` was opened when no config file existed, with a `FutureWarning`. Since 0.21.0 it is not: if one is there and the new default is not, `spice-kernel-db` raises `LegacyDatabaseFound` naming the move command, rather than quietly starting an empty database beside it.

`kernel_roots` is the list of kernel roots used to guess a mission from a path. When it is `None` (the default) the roots are read from the configuration the first time they are needed. The resolved list is available as the `db.kernel_roots` property. Pass it to keep a script independent of the user's configuration.

Set `read_only=True` for commands that only query the database. Several read-only connections can be open at once, but DuckDB's file lock means none can open while another process has the database open for writing (for example during `get`); that raises `duckdb.IOException`.

### Mission management

#### `add_mission`

```python
db.add_mission(
    name: str,
    server_url: str,
    mk_dir_url: str,
    dedup: bool = True,
) -> None
```

Register a mission. If it already exists, replaces the existing entry.

#### `list_missions`

```python
db.list_missions() -> list[dict]
```

List all configured missions. Returns dicts with keys: `name`, `server_url`, `server_label`, `mk_dir_url`, `dedup`, `added_at`.

#### `remove_mission`

```python
db.remove_mission(name: str) -> bool
```

Remove a mission. Returns True if found and removed, False if not found.

#### `get_mission`

```python
db.get_mission(name: str) -> dict | None
```

Look up a mission by name (case-insensitive). Returns dict with same keys as `list_missions`, or None.

---

### Scanning

#### `scan_directory`

```python
db.scan_directory(
    root: str | Path,
    mission: str | None = None,
    extensions: set[str] | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
    archive: bool = False,
    archive_roots: dict[str, Path] | None = None,
) -> tuple[int, set[str]]
```

Recursively scan a directory tree and register all kernel files. Returns `(count, missions_found)` — the number of files registered and a set of detected mission names.

With `archive=True`, each file is moved into a kernel root, laid out as `{root}/{mission}/{type}/{filename}`, and a symlink is left at the original location. The root is the file's own when it already sits in a configured root, else `root_for` of its mission. Every file's root is settled before anything moves, so an `AmbiguousKernelRoot` leaves the tree untouched; `archive_roots` (`{mission: root}`) answers it on the next call. `scan_roots` takes the same two arguments.

If `mission` is not provided, it is detected from the path with [`guess_mission`](#guess_mission) and the database's kernel roots: under a root, the first directory below the root; elsewhere, the path structure (`.../<MISSION>/kernels/...`). `register_file` guesses the same way when it is given no mission.

`extensions` defaults to all known SPICE kernel extensions (`.tls`, `.tpc`, `.bsp`, `.bc`, `.tf`, `.ti`, `.tsc`, `.bds`, `.tm`).

#### `scan_roots`

```python
db.scan_roots(
    verbose: bool = False,
    archive: bool = False,
    archive_roots: dict[str, Path] | None = None,
) -> tuple[int, set[str]]
```

Run `scan_directory` over every kernel root in `db.kernel_roots`, in order, as `skd scan` does with no directory. Returns the total count and the union of the missions found. A root that is not an existing directory is skipped with the message `Kernel root <path> does not exist; skipped.`

#### `register_file`

```python
db.register_file(
    path: str | Path,
    mission: str | None = None,
    source_url: str | None = None,
    archive_dir: str | Path | None = None,
    expected_hash: str | None = None,
) -> str
```

Register a single kernel file. Returns its SHA-256 hash.

If `archive_dir` is provided, the file is moved into the archive and a symlink is left at the original location. If `expected_hash` is provided, the computed hash is verified before storing — raises `ValueError` on mismatch.

If the file's content already exists in the database under a different filename, the new location is recorded pointing to the same hash. This is logged at the `INFO` level.

---

### Lookup

#### `resolve_metakernel`

```python
db.resolve_metakernel(ref: str | Path, mission: str | None = None) -> Path
```

The on-disk path of the metakernel *ref* names. *ref* may be a path that exists, a registry filename, a registry `mk_path`, the `source_url` it was fetched from, or a version-stripped base name (`juice_crema_5_2.tm` for `juice_crema_5_2_v473_20260819_001.tm`), case-insensitive, with or without `.tm`; *mission* narrows the registry to one mission (prefix match). Every CLI command resolves its metakernel argument through this method, so a name works the same everywhere.

Raises `MetakernelNotTracked` when nothing matches or the matched file is gone, and `AmbiguousMetakernel` when several registry rows match; it never picks the first of several.

#### `registry_rows`

```python
db.registry_rows(mission: str | None = None) -> list[RegistryRow]
```

Every tracked metakernel as a `RegistryRow`, ordered by mission and filename; *mission* is a case-insensitive prefix filter. The one registry query behind the resolver and the CLI pickers. `official` is `False` for a metakernel imported with `official=False` and `True` otherwise. The column is added when a database from before this release is first opened for writing. Opened read-only (`ls`, `show`, `doctor`, `check`) before that, every row reads as official.


#### `RegistryRow`

A `NamedTuple` with one tracked metakernel's registry row: `mk_path` (the file on disk), `source_url` (where `get` fetched it, `None` for a scanned or imported file), `filename`, `mission`, `acquired_at` and `official`. Returned by `registry_rows` and `registry_row`; part of the public API because the module-level functions and planetarypy read it.

#### `find_by_filename`

```python
db.find_by_filename(filename: str) -> list[dict]
```

Find all locations for a kernel by filename (basename). Checks both the canonical filename in the `kernels` table and the actual filename in `locations.abs_path`.

Returns a list of dicts with keys: `sha256`, `abs_path`, `mission`, `kernel_type`, `size_bytes`.

#### `find_by_hash`

```python
db.find_by_hash(sha256: str) -> list[dict]
```

Find all locations for a kernel by its SHA-256 hash.

Returns a list of dicts with keys: `abs_path`, `mission`, `filename`.

#### `resolve_kernel`

```python
db.resolve_kernel(
    filename: str,
    preferred_mission: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[str | None, list[str]]
```

Resolve a kernel filename to an absolute path on disk.

Returns `(path, warnings)` where `path` is the resolved absolute path (or `None` if not found) and `warnings` is a list of human-readable strings about any fallback decisions.

**Resolution priority** (see [Mission-aware resolution](design.qmd#mission-aware-resolution)):

1. Exact filename match in `preferred_mission` → no warning
2. Exact filename match in any mission → warning
3. Path-suffix match (file on disk registered under different name) → warning
4. Metakernel registry match, for `.tm` files acquired via `get` → warning only on a cross-mission hit
5. Not found → `(None, [])` + hint to run `scan`

Steps 1 and 2 match on content, so a name can have several hits when two
byte-identical files are registered under different names. A location actually
named `filename` always wins; a differently-named copy is used only when no
file of the requested name is registered, and says so in a warning.

#### `aliases`

```python
db.aliases(name_or_hash: str) -> dict | None
```

Follow the deduplication trail for a kernel. `name_or_hash` may be a full or partial (≥6-char) SHA-256, the canonical filename, or *any* alias filename the content has been registered under.

Returns `None` if nothing matches, otherwise a dict:

```python
{
    "sha256": str,
    "canonical": str,          # first-seen filename (kernels.filename)
    "kernel_type": str,
    "size_bytes": int,
    "superseded": bool,
    "aliases": list[str],      # every filename this content is known under
    "locations": list[dict],   # {"abs_path", "mission", "source_url"}
}
```

Aliases are **derived from `locations`**, not stored separately: the read-only view `kernel_aliases (sha256, filename)` exposes every distinct on-disk basename each content hash appears under, so a deduplicated kernel (identical bytes under several names) is followable with zero extra bookkeeping — the trade-off is that a name is forgotten once its file is pruned. The companion `alias_counts(shas: list[str]) -> dict[str, int]` maps each hash to its number of known names, and `alias_counts_by_name(filenames: list[str]) -> dict[str, int]` maps each filename to how many *other* names its content is known under (used to render the `(+N aliases)` annotation in kernel listings).

### Metakernel operations

#### `check_metakernel`

```python
db.check_metakernel(
    mk_path: str | Path,
    mission: str | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> dict
```

Check which kernels from a metakernel are available locally.

Returns a dict with keys:

- `found`: list of `(raw_entry, local_path)` tuples
- `missing`: list of `raw_entry` strings
- `warnings`: list of warning strings

#### `rewrite_metakernel`

```python
db.rewrite_metakernel(
    mk_path: str | Path,
    output: str | Path,
    *,
    mission: str | None = None,
    link_root: str | Path | None = None,
) -> tuple[Path, list[str]]
```

Rewrite a metakernel for local use with minimal edits.

Creates a symlink tree at `link_root` (default: `kernels/` next to the output file) that mirrors the original directory structure. Only `PATH_VALUES` in the output `.tm` file is changed — `KERNELS_TO_LOAD`, `PATH_SYMBOLS`, and all comments are preserved.

Returns `(output_path, warnings)`.

See [Minimal metakernel edits](design.qmd#minimal-edits) for the design rationale.

#### `get_metakernel`

```python
db.get_metakernel(
    url: str,
    download_dir: str | Path | None = None,
    mission: str | None = None,
    yes: bool = False,
    force: bool = False,
    verbose: bool = False,
    dry_run: bool = False,
) -> dict
```

Fetch a remote metakernel, display a status table, and download missing kernels.

1. Fetches and parses the remote `.tm` file
2. Resolves kernel entries to full URLs (using `PATH_VALUES` relative to the metakernel URL)
3. Checks each kernel against the local database
4. Queries remote file sizes via parallel HTTP HEAD requests
5. Shows a summary table with kernel names, sizes, and status (`in db` / `missing`) on the instance's console
6. Asks for confirmation on that console (unless `yes=True`); with no console there is nobody to ask, so the call stops after the status step like `dry_run`, writes nothing, and the result carries `aborted: True`
7. Downloads missing kernels, preserving subdirectory structure, and registers them
8. Creates symlinks for kernels already in the database so the metakernel works immediately

`download_dir` defaults to `root_for(mission)`: the configured root that already holds kernels of the mission, or the only configured root. With several roots and no such fact it raises `AmbiguousKernelRoot` rather than guess; pass `download_dir` then. Downloaded files are placed under `<download_dir>/<mission>/<relpath>`.

`verbose=True` additionally lists each kernel's resolved URL beneath the status table. The table is shown whenever there is a console: it precedes the download question, so it is what you decide on.

`dry_run=True` stops after the status table. Nothing is written to disk or to the database and no kernel is downloaded. This is what `skd update` runs without `--execute`.

Returns a dict with keys: `found`, `missing`, `downloaded`, `warnings`. After a dry run the dict also has `dry_run: True`, and `downloaded` is empty.

#### `update_metakernel`

```python
db.update_metakernel(
    mk_path_or_name: str | Path,
    mission: str | None = None,
    download_dir: str | Path | None = None,
    yes: bool = False,
    force: bool = False,
    verbose: bool = False,
    dry_run: bool = False,
    rescan: bool = True,
) -> dict
```

Re-fetch a metakernel from its source URL and download new or missing kernels. Looks up the source URL from the `metakernel_registry`, falling back to the mission's `mk_dir_url` + filename if no source URL is stored.

Raises `LookupError` if the metakernel is not found in the registry or was added via scan without a source URL. Raises `MetakernelUnreachableError` (a `LookupError` subclass) when the remote returns 403/404/410 — typically because NAIF rotated the file into `former_versions/`; use `prune_metakernels()` to clean up the stale registry row.

After downloading, automatically rescans the kernel directories referenced by the metakernel so newly downloaded files are immediately indexed. `verbose=True` names each directory as it is re-scanned; otherwise the count is reported in one line. `rescan=False` skips that step; `update_all` uses it and scans each distinct directory once at the end.

`dry_run=True` reports what would change and writes nothing. No rescan happens after a dry run.

Returns the same dict as `get_metakernel`. After a real run the dict also has `scan_dirs`, the set of directories the metakernel points at.

#### `update_all`

```python
db.update_all(dry_run: bool = False, verbose: bool = False) -> list[dict]
```

Re-fetch every tracked metakernel from its source, as `skd update` does. Each one lands in the root that holds it (`root_for`); there is no directory argument. With `dry_run=True` each metakernel's status table is shown and nothing is written. With `dry_run=False` the missing kernels are downloaded without a per-metakernel prompt, and the directories the metakernels point at are re-indexed once at the end. The `skd update` command passes `dry_run=True` unless `--execute` is given.

Alias rows, where a symlink stands next to its target, are skipped. A source that has gone from the server, a source that cannot be reached, and a row with no source URL are reported in the summary table and never raise.

Returns one dict per metakernel walked, with keys `filename`, `mission`, `count` and `error`. `count` is the number of missing kernels in a dry run and the number of downloaded kernels otherwise. `error` is `None` or a one-line reason.

#### `import_metakernel`

```python
db.import_metakernel(mk_path: str | Path, mission: str | None = None, official: bool = True) -> dict
```

Track a metakernel that is already on disk, without a download, as `skd import` does. Indexes its entries, registers every kernel it resolves to that exists on disk, and adds the registry row with no source URL. `mission` defaults to the mission guessed from the path, with the configured kernel roots taken into account (see [`guess_mission`](#guess_mission)).

`official=False` marks a metakernel assembled locally, such as a subsetter's output or the one planetarypy builds in `archived_kernels.py`, as `skd import --unofficial` does. The flag is stored in the registry, `ls` appends `unofficial` to the name, and `show` prints `Official: no`. Importing a path again replaces its row, so the flag follows the latest call.

Returns a dict with keys `mk_path`, `filename`, `mission`, `n_entries`, `n_registered` and `missing`, the entries whose file is not on disk. Raises `FileNotFoundError` when `mk_path` is not a file.

#### `verify_metakernel`

```python
db.verify_metakernel(
    mk_path: str | Path,
    *,
    deep: bool = False,
) -> dict
```

Deeply cross-check a metakernel against the database. Each entry in `KERNELS_TO_LOAD` is substituted through `PATH_VALUES`/`PATH_SYMBOLS` to an absolute path and validated against the `kernels` row of the registered location at that path, or of the file a symlink there leads to. Only a path the database has not registered falls back to the `kernels` rows whose filename matches (case-insensitive).

Checks: traversal escape from `PATH_VALUES` root, dangling symlinks, missing files, size mismatch, SHA-256 mismatch (only in `deep` mode), `AMBIGUOUS` resolution (the path is not registered and multiple non-superseded `kernels` rows share the filename; a registered path is never ambiguous, so a same-named kernel with other content in another mission or kernel root is not flagged — see [`superseded_by` semantics](design.qmd)), unregistered files, and non-absolute `PATH_VALUES`.

Returns a dict with keys `entries`, `ok`, `fail`, `fatal`, `mk_path`, `deep`. Each entry is a dict with `raw`, `resolved`, `status`, `detail`. `fatal` is `True` if any entry is in a P0 state (e.g. `TRAVERSAL`, `HASH_MISMATCH`, `AMBIGUOUS`).

This is the recommended cross-check after every `get`/`update`/`rewrite`. Run with `deep=True` periodically to catch content corruption that preserves size.

#### `prune_orphan_symlinks`

```python
db.prune_orphan_symlinks(dry_run: bool = True) -> list[str]
```

Walk every mission's download tree (derived from
`metakernel_registry.mk_path` — the parent of the `mk/` directory) and
find symlinks whose target no longer exists. These accumulate when an
underlying kernel store moves or after `db.prune()` removes a
`locations` row — the symlinks pointing at that file are not themselves
tracked in `locations`, so they survive as junk.

With `dry_run=False`, every dangling symlink is unlinked. Healthy
symlinks and regular files are left alone.

Returns a list of absolute paths that were (or would be) removed.

#### `prune_metakernels`

```python
db.prune_metakernels(
    dry_run: bool = True,
    delete_files: bool = False,
    timeout: float = 10.0,
) -> list[dict]
```

Find rows in `metakernel_registry` whose remote URL returns a permanent HTTP error (403/404/410) and optionally remove them. Sends a HEAD request to each URL with the given `timeout`.

The probe URL is derived per row: explicit `source_url` if set, otherwise `mission.mk_dir_url + filename` (same fallback as `update_metakernel`). Rows with neither — typically locally-created metakernels with no upstream — are noted in the output and skipped (use `skd rm <name>` to drop them manually).

Transient failures (timeouts, DNS errors, 5xx) are deliberately **never** classified as dead — leaving a registry row stale is always safer than deleting on a network blip.

With `dry_run=False`, the matching rows are removed from `metakernel_registry` and `metakernel_entries`. With `delete_files=True`, the on-disk `.tm` file is also unlinked; symlink trees under the mission's download directory are shared and never auto-cleaned.

Returns a list of dicts, one per dead metakernel: `{'mk_path', 'filename', 'mission', 'source_url', 'status_code'}`.

#### `index_metakernel`

```python
db.index_metakernel(mk_path: str | Path)
```

Parse a metakernel and store its entries in the `metakernel_entries` table for future reference.

#### `list_metakernels`

```python
db.list_metakernels(mission: str | None = None, show: bool = True) -> list[dict]
```

List all tracked metakernels, optionally filtered by mission. Each entry includes the number of kernel entries.

Alias rows (symlink metakernels created by `get`) inherit their target's entry count and content fingerprint, so the listing reads consistently — both rows show the same kernel count and one of them is annotated `↳ identical to <target>`.

Shows a summary table on the instance's console (`show=False` suppresses it even with a console; planetarypy's released code passes it) and returns a list of dicts with keys: `filename`, `mission`, `source_url`, `acquired_at`, `mk_path`, `n_kernels`, `official`, plus `identical_to` (set when another row has the same content fingerprint).

#### `metakernels_covering`

```python
db.metakernels_covering(body_id: int, et: float | None = None, mission: str | None = None) -> list[dict]
```

Tracked metakernels whose SPK kernels cover a body, for code that needs to pick a metakernel rather than show one. Prints nothing and writes nothing, so it works with `read_only=True`. Coverage is read from the SPK files each metakernel loads (those present on disk); identical aliases are skipped. With `et`, only metakernels covering that ephemeris time are returned; without it, any coverage counts.

Returns the `list_metakernels` rows with an added `intervals` key, the `(et_start, et_end)` windows for the body. Needs SpiceyPy.

```python
import spiceypy
db = KernelDB(read_only=True)
spiceypy.furnsh("naif0012.tls")
rows = db.metakernels_covering(-121, spiceypy.utc2et("2027-06-01"))   # BepiColombo MPO
```

#### `info_metakernel`

```python
db.info_metakernel(name: str, kernel_type: str | None = None) -> dict
```

Show detailed info about a tracked metakernel, as `skd show` does. `name` is any form `resolve_metakernel` accepts. Displays per-kernel status (`in db` / `missing`) with kernel type and size. `kernel_type` limits the printed kernel table to one type; the counts stay whole.

Returns a dict with keys: `filename`, `mission`, `source_url`, `acquired_at`, `mk_path`, `official`, `kernels`, `n_kernels`, `n_in_db`, `n_missing`. Raises `MetakernelNotTracked` if nothing matches.

#### `browse_remote_metakernels`

```python
db.browse_remote_metakernels(
    mk_dir_url: str,
    mission: str | None = None,
    show_versioned: bool = False,
    sort_by: str = "name",
    filter: str | None = None,
) -> list[dict]
```

Scan a remote NAIF `mk/` directory and show available metakernels. Groups entries by base name (stripping version tags like `_v461_20251127_001`), counts versioned snapshots, and checks which base metakernels have been locally acquired.

`sort_by` controls row ordering: `"name"` (default) sorts alphabetically; `"date"` sorts by latest remote modification date ascending, so the most recently updated metakernels appear at the bottom.

`filter` is an optional case-insensitive substring applied to entry filenames before grouping. Useful for narrowing large listings such as the ~1,400-entry JUICE `former_versions/` archive.

Prints a summary table and returns a list of dicts with keys: `base_name`, `n_versions`, `latest_date`, `is_local`, `filenames`.

---

### Deduplication

#### `report_duplicates`

```python
db.report_duplicates(min_copies: int = 2) -> list[dict]
```

Find and report kernels that exist in multiple locations.

Returns a list of dicts with keys: `sha256`, `filename`, `size_bytes`, `count`, `paths`, `missions`, `wasted_bytes`.

#### `deduplicate_plan`

```python
db.deduplicate_plan() -> list[dict]
```

Generate a deduplication plan without executing it.

For each set of identical files, selects a canonical copy (preferring `generic` mission) and lists the rest as removable. Respects per-mission dedup settings from the `missions` table.

Returns a list of dicts with keys: `filename`, `size_bytes`, `keep`, `remove`.

#### `deduplicate_with_symlinks`

```python
db.deduplicate_with_symlinks(dry_run: bool = True) -> list[dict]
```

Replace duplicate files with symlinks to the canonical copy.

With `dry_run=True` (the default), only prints what would happen.

---

### Statistics

#### `check_report`

```python
db.check_report(mk_path, *, mission=None, hash_=False, remote=False, spice=False) -> dict
```

Everything the `check` command reports, as data: `mk_path`, the raw results under `present` (`check_metakernel`), `resolves` (`verify_metakernel`, SHA-256 with `hash_`) and `remote` (`verify_against_server`, only with `remote`, the one network path, together with `newer`, the newer-version notice or `None`), the three `verdicts` as `{bit, ok, line}` rows and `exit_code`, the sum of the failed verdicts' bits. `check_metakernel` itself prints nothing and touches no network.

#### `stale_locations`

```python
db.stale_locations() -> list[tuple[str, str]]
```

`(sha256, abs_path)` of every location whose file is gone from disk; the one walk behind `clean` and `doctor`.

#### `doctor`

```python
db.doctor() -> dict
```

Database health with no metakernel argument: `n_kernels`, `n_locations`, `n_metakernels`, `poisoned` (the `poisoned_superseded()` rows), `missing_locations` (location paths whose file is gone), `conflicting_locations` (paths with more than one `locations` row, that is one file registered under more than one hash) and `missing_metakernels` (registry filenames whose file is gone). The CLI's `doctor` prints it and exits 1 only when `poisoned` is non-empty. A `scan_directory` of the directory holding a conflicting path keeps the row that matches the file on disk and supersedes the others; `register_file` supersedes every stale row at the path, not only one.

#### `poisoned_superseded`

```python
db.poisoned_superseded() -> list[dict]
```

Kernels flagged as superseded by content that exists in no live location, while their own file is present on disk. These resolve as "not found" and re-download on every `update`; `scan` over the kernel directory repairs them. A genuine upstream update whose newer file is on disk is not listed.

Returns one dict per kernel with keys: `sha256`, `filename`, `superseded_by`, `abs_path`.

#### `stats`

```python
db.stats() -> dict
```

Print and return summary statistics.

Returns a dict with keys: `n_kernels`, `n_locations`, `total_bytes`, `n_duplicates`, `n_poisoned`, `missions`.

### `ParsedMetakernel`

Dataclass with attributes:

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `source_path` | `Path` | Absolute path to the source file |

| `path_symbols` | `list[str]` | Contents of `PATH_SYMBOLS` |

Properties and methods:

| Name | Returns | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `symbol_map` | `dict[str, str]` | Mapping from symbol name to path value |
| `resolve(entry)` | `str` | Replace `$SYMBOL`s with their values |
| `kernel_filenames()` | `list[str]` | Basenames of all kernels |
| `kernel_relpaths()` | `list[str]` | Relative paths with `$SYMBOL` stripped |

## Configuration

```python
from spice_kernel_db import (
    Config, ConfigError, ensure_config, kernel_roots, add_root, remove_root,
)
```

Nothing in this module prints or prompts. The first-run questions and the `skd config` display belong to the CLI.

### `ensure_config`

```python
ensure_config(seed_root: str | Path | None = None) -> Config
```

Load the configuration from `~/.config/spice-kernel-db/config.toml`. With `seed_root` and no config file yet, it writes a configuration with the default database path and `seed_root` as the first kernel root, and creates both directories. An existing configuration is never changed by `seed_root`. A library such as planetarypy calls it this way on first run to point skd at its own store.

With no file and no `seed_root` it raises `ConfigError` naming `spice-kernel-db config --setup`, the command that asks for the paths. A file that does not parse also raises `ConfigError`, never reads as "not configured".

### `Config`

```python
Config(db_path=DEFAULT_DB_PATH, kernel_dirs=[DEFAULT_KERNEL_DIR])
```

Configuration object with these attributes:

| Attribute | Type | Default | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `db_path` | `str` | `~/.local/share/spice-kernel-db/kernels.duckdb` | Path to the DuckDB database |
| `kernel_dirs` | `list[str]` | `["~/.local/share/spice-kernel-db/kernels"]` | The kernel roots. No root is special; see `root_for` below. Never empty: an empty list becomes the default store. |

The `[storage]` section of the file holds `kernel_dirs`, and `save_config` writes only that key. A file written before the list existed has only `kernel_dir`; it loads as a one-root list and is rewritten as `kernel_dirs` on the next save.

### Kernel roots

```python
kernel_roots(config: Config | None = None) -> list[Path]
add_root(directory: str | Path, config: Config | None = None) -> Config
remove_root(directory: str | Path, config: Config | None = None) -> Config
```

`kernel_roots` returns the configured roots as expanded, resolved paths. Without a config file it returns the one default root. Pass `config` to avoid reading the file a second time. `add_root` and `remove_root` take the same `config` argument and edit that object instead of loading the file.

`add_root` appends `directory` to the roots and saves. It creates the directory when missing and does not add a root twice; the order of the others is kept. It runs no prompt, and without a config file it writes one with the default database path. It returns the updated `Config`.

`remove_root` removes `directory` from the roots and saves. It raises `ValueError` when the directory is not a root or is the last one. Files on disk and database rows are untouched; `clean` drops rows whose file is gone. It returns the updated `Config`.

```python
from spice_kernel_db import add_root, kernel_roots

add_root("~/planetarypy_data/spice_kernels")
kernel_roots()
# [PosixPath('/Users/me/.local/share/spice-kernel-db/kernels'),
#  PosixPath('/Users/me/planetarypy_data/spice_kernels')]
```

The CLI equivalents are `skd config add-root` and `skd config remove-root`; see [Several kernel roots](cli.qmd#several-kernel-roots).

### `KernelDB.root_for`

```python
db.root_for(mission: str | None, mk_path: str | Path | None = None) -> Path
```

The one answer to "which kernel root does this download belong in". In order: the root that contains `mk_path` (a tracked metakernel is re-fetched into its own store), the only configured root, and the one root that already holds kernels of `mission`. When several roots remain it raises `AmbiguousKernelRoot` (a `LookupError` carrying `mission` and `roots`) instead of picking the first; the CLI turns that into a picker at a terminal and exit 2 in a script. `get_metakernel` and `update_metakernel` call it when `download_dir` is not given (a URL that is already tracked uses that row's root), and `scan_directory(archive=True)` calls it for every file outside the roots.

### `guess_mission`

```python
from spice_kernel_db.hashing import guess_mission

guess_mission(filepath: str, roots: list[Path] | None = None) -> str
```

Best-effort mission name for a kernel file, canonicalized like every stored mission name. Under one of `roots` (as returned by `kernel_roots()`) the mission is the first directory below the root, because skd's own store is laid out as `<root>/<MISSION>/<type>/<file>`. A file under a root but not in a mission directory, for example directly in the root or in a type directory such as `mk`, is classified from its filename only. Outside every root the path heuristic applies: the directory before `kernels/`, then the parent of a kernel-type directory, then filename patterns.

`register_file`, `scan_directory` and `import_metakernel` pass `db.kernel_roots`. `check_metakernel`, `rewrite_metakernel`, `coverage_metakernel` and the server comparison do not guess for a tracked metakernel: when `mission` is not given they read it from the registry row, and only an untracked file is guessed from its path.

## Remote utilities

Internal since 0.23 (#49): importable from `spice_kernel_db.remote`, not part of the public API above.

```python
from spice_kernel_db.remote import fetch_metakernel, resolve_kernel_urls
```

### `fetch_metakernel`

```python
fetch_metakernel(url: str) -> str
```

Download and return the text content of a remote metakernel file.

### `resolve_kernel_urls`

```python
resolve_kernel_urls(mk_url: str, parsed: ParsedMetakernel) -> list[str]
```

Resolve each `KERNELS_TO_LOAD` entry in a parsed metakernel to a full URL, using `PATH_VALUES` relative to the metakernel's own URL.

### `list_remote_missions`

```python
from spice_kernel_db.remote import list_remote_missions
list_remote_missions(server_url: str) -> list[str]
```

List available mission directories from a SPICE archive server (NASA NAIF or ESA SPICE). Parses the Apache directory listing.

### `SPICE_SERVERS`

```python
from spice_kernel_db.remote import SPICE_SERVERS
```

Dict mapping server labels to URLs: `{"NASA": "https://naif.jpl.nasa.gov/pub/naif/", "ESA": "https://spiftp.esac.esa.int/data/SPICE/"}`.

### `list_remote_metakernels`

```python
from spice_kernel_db.remote import list_remote_metakernels
```

```python
list_remote_metakernels(mk_dir_url: str) -> list[RemoteMetakernel]
```

Parse an Apache directory listing at *mk_dir_url* and extract `.tm` metakernel entries. For each file, computes a `base_name` by stripping NAIF version tags (e.g. `_v461_20251127_001`). Returns a list sorted by `(base_name, filename)`.

### `RemoteMetakernel`

Dataclass with attributes:

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `filename` | `str` | Original filename from the directory listing |
| `url` | `str` | Full URL to the file |
| `date` | `str` | Last modified date from the listing |
| `size` | `str` | Size string from the listing (e.g. `"12K"`) |
| `base_name` | `str` | Filename with version tag stripped |
| `version_tag` | `str \| None` | Version tag (e.g. `"v461_20251127_001"`) or `None` |

### `probe_mk_candidates`

```python
from spice_kernel_db.remote import probe_mk_candidates
probe_mk_candidates(urls: list[str], *, max_workers: int = 8, timeout: float = 5.0) -> list[str]
```

Send parallel HEAD requests to candidate metakernel-directory URLs and return those that respond successfully, preserving the input order (which encodes priority). Duplicates are collapsed.

### `discover_mk_url`

```python
from spice_kernel_db.remote import discover_mk_url, DEFAULT_ALT_MK_PATHS
discover_mk_url(
    server_url: str,
    mission: str,
    *,
    registry_candidates: list[str] | None = None,
    extra_paths: tuple[str, ...] = DEFAULT_ALT_MK_PATHS,
    timeout: float = 5.0,
) -> list[str]
```

Discover live metakernel directory URLs for *mission*. Tries `registry_candidates` (highest priority) first, then expands the templates in `extra_paths` (placeholders `{server}` and `{m}`). Returns hits in priority order.

`DEFAULT_ALT_MK_PATHS` contains only `{server}{m}/kernels/mk/`. An empirical NAIF survey found that no missions use alternative templates one might expect from naming convention — alternates should be added via the curated registry or `--mk-dir-url`, not inferred.

## Mission registry

```python
from spice_kernel_db import registry
```

Reads `mission_registry.toml` shipped with the package. Used by `mission add` to find metakernel directories for missions whose layout deviates from the default.

### `MissionEntry`

Dataclass with one field, `candidates: tuple[str, ...]`: URL templates with `{server}`/`{m}` placeholders.

### `load_registry`

```python
registry.load_registry() -> dict[str, MissionEntry]
```

Cached loader for the bundled registry. Clear the cache via `registry.load_registry.cache_clear()` after replacing the data file (only relevant in tests).

### `registry_candidates`

```python
registry.registry_candidates(mission: str, server_url: str) -> list[str]
```

Return registry-defined candidate metakernel URLs for *mission* with placeholders expanded. Empty list when the mission has no registry entry.

## Exceptions

```python
from spice_kernel_db import (
    AmbiguousKernelRoot,
    AmbiguousMetakernel,
    ConcurrentModificationError,
    ConfigError,
    LegacyDatabaseFound,
    MetakernelNotTracked,
    MetakernelUnreachableError,
)
```

### `ConfigError`

Raised by `load_config` and `ensure_config` when the config file does not parse, or when there is no file and no `seed_root` to write one from. Subclass of `RuntimeError` (not `ValueError`, which `remove_root` uses for a bad argument). The CLI prints the message and exits 78, the conventional code for a configuration error, outside the 0 to 7 that `check` uses as verdict bits; `spice-kernel-db config --setup` writes a fresh file.

### `LegacyDatabaseFound`

Raised by `KernelDB()` when no config file exists and a database sits at the pre-0.19 default `~/.spice_kernels.duckdb`; the message names the move command. Subclass of `RuntimeError`.

### `AmbiguousKernelRoot`

Raised by `KernelDB.root_for()` (and so by `get_metakernel`, `update_metakernel` and `scan_directory(archive=True)`) when several kernel roots are configured and nothing says which one a mission's download belongs in: no root holds the metakernel or kernels of that mission. Subclass of `LookupError`. Attributes: `mission`, `roots` (the candidates), `stored` (whether the mission is in more than one root). The CLI shows a picker at a terminal and exits 2 otherwise; `--download-dir` is the explicit answer.

### `AmbiguousMetakernel`

Raised by `KernelDB.resolve_metakernel()` (and so by every method that takes a metakernel reference) when the reference matches several registry rows, for example a base name while two versioned snapshots are tracked. Subclass of `LookupError`. Attributes: `name`, `candidates` (the matching registry filenames). The CLI lists the candidates and exits 2.

### `MetakernelNotTracked`

Raised when a metakernel reference matches nothing in the registry and is not a path on disk, or when the matched registry row points at a file that is gone. Subclass of `LookupError`. Attribute: `name`. The message carries the `spice-kernel-db get <name>` hint; the CLI prints it and exits 1.

### `ConcurrentModificationError`

Raised when `KernelDB.get_metakernel()` detects that another process modified the kernel records during its network I/O window (after the DB lock was released to allow parallel reads). Subclass of `RuntimeError`. Retry the operation after the other writer completes.

### `MetakernelUnreachableError`

Raised by `KernelDB.update_metakernel()` when the remote metakernel returns HTTP 403/404/410 — typically because NAIF rotated the file into `former_versions/`. Subclass of `LookupError`. Attributes: `url`, `status` (int HTTP code), `filename`. Recovery: `db.prune_metakernels(dry_run=False)`.
